title: Isolation of a chloride-capped cerium polyoxo nanocluster built from 52 metal ions

synthesis.procedure: In the shared preparation, ceric ammonium nitrate (0.247–0.274 g, approximately 0.5 mmol) was dissolved in water to approximately 0.5 M Ce(IV). Excess aqueous ammonium hydroxide precipitated a yellow solid. After centrifugation and washing with water (2 × 2 mL), the pellet was dissolved over several hours in 1 mL of 1 M HCl. An aliquot of this stock (25 μL, approximately 0.013 mmol Ce) was combined with 200 μL of 1 M HCl and pyridine (5 μL, 0.062 mmol) in a 3 mL shell vial. The solution evaporated slowly over several days under ambient conditions in a fume hood. Ce1-1 crystallized when the solution reached complete dryness.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A discrete core of 38 cerium sites bridged by oxo groups is surface-decorated by 50 chloride ions and 12 coordinated water molecules. The core adopts a fluorite-type cerium oxide arrangement.

properties.summary: Single-crystal UV–vis–NIR absorption shows a visible band attributed to ligand-to-metal charge transfer and a near-infrared intervalence charge-transfer feature consistent with mixed Ce(III)/Ce(IV). The main text places the near-infrared peak at approximately 1200 nm, whereas the SI caption describes a band centered around 1100 nm.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The crystal contains two crystallographically distinct 52-cerium clusters with different surface chloride/water counts: [Ce52O80−x(OH)xCl60(H2O)16] and [Ce52O80−x(OH)xCl58(H2O)18]. The described cluster has an A:B:C:B:A cerium-layer arrangement (6:12:16:12:6), comprising a fluorite-type Ce24 core, two Ce6 units, and four Ce4 units; chloride and water terminate its surface.
